'''Yuri Andreevich Yappa''' ({{langx|ru|Юрий Андреевич Яппа}}) (September 21, 1927 &ndash; August 19, 1998) was a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] and [[Russia]]n theoretical physicist. He is known for publications on [[particle physics]], [[quantum field theory]], [[General Relativity]], [[philosophy of science]], and for his graduate texts on [[classical electrodynamics]] and theory of [[spinor]]s.

== Biography ==
Yuri Yappa was born in [[Saint Petersburg|Leningrad]], [[USSR]] in the family of doctor Andrei Yappa ({{langx|de|Andreas Jappa}}, {{langx|ru|[[:ru:Андрей Яппа|Андрей Яппа]]}}).

In 1941, because of the [[Operation Barbarossa|German invasion]] in the Soviet Union and the [[Siege of Leningrad]] he had to interrupt his regular education and to start working. During the whole Siege of Leningrad he worked at the hospital where his father also worked. In 1944, he was awarded of [[medal "For the Defence of Leningrad"]]. In parallel with the work in the hospital, he continued his self-education, so that in 1944 he passed exams for the entire course of the school and started to study at the Physical Faculty of the [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad University]]. During the winter of 1944-1945 he with a few other students alternated their studies with a work as stokers in the university's boiler-house.<ref>{{Cite journal
 |url=http://www.spbumag.nw.ru/2004/14/5.shtml
 |author=Шухтина, М.А.
 |script-title=ru:Как МейБоДо сохранили непрерывность образования на физическом факультете
 |journal=Санкт-Петербургский университет
 |language=ru
 |trans-title=How "MeiBoDo" Preserved the Continuity of Education at the Physical Faculty
 |issue=14–15
 |pages=1671–72
 |date=2004-05-21
 |archive-date=2014-04-13
 |access-date=2014-04-12
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413125007/http://www.spbumag.nw.ru/2004/14/5.shtml
 |url-status=dead
 }}</ref> Yuri Yappa also started to work at the laboratory of [[molecular physics]], but later, following an advice of its head Viktor Tsvetkov, joined a [[theoretical physics]] group.

In 1949 he graduated from the Leningrad University, then continued postgraduate studies there at the chair of theoretical physics headed by [[Vladimir Fock]]. Since then Yuri Yappa was the nearest collaborator of Vladimir Fock till the death of the latter in 1974.

== Academic career ==
In 1953 Yuri Yappa earned his PhD ({{langx|ru|кандидат наук}}) degree with a thesis on the relativistic theory of elementary particles.<ref>{{cite book
 |author=Яппа Ю. А.
 |year=1953
 |script-title=ru:Шредингеровские формы релятивистски-инвариантных уравнений для элементарных частиц и некоторые вопросы их физической интерпретации
 |location=Ленинград
 |publisher=Лениградский государственный университет
 |language=ru
 |trans-title=Schrödinger Forms of Relativistically Invariant Equations for Elementary Particles and Some Problems of Their Physical Interpretation (PhD Thesis)
}}</ref>

[[File:Yappa57.jpg|thumb|Yuri Yappa in 1957.]]
In 1954–1956, he led a group of theoreticians at the Institute of Nuclear Problems of the [[Soviet Academy of Sciences]] in [[Dubna]] ([[Moscow Region]]). His group worked on the theory of [[elementary particles]] and provided theoretical explanation of experimental results on [[proton]] [[scattering]]. In the same period he also edited two collective monographs in the series "Problems of Modern Physics".<ref>{{cite book
 |year=1955
 |script-title=ru:Систематика элементарных частиц
 |editor=Ю. А. Яппа
 |series=Проблемы современной физики
 |volume=10
 |location=Москва
 |publisher=Издательство иностранной литературы
 |language=ru
 |trans-title=Systematics of Elementary Particles
}}</ref><ref>{{cite book
 |year=1956
 |script-title=ru:Метод Тамма–Данкова
 |editor=Ю. А. Яппа
 |series=Проблемы современной физики
 |volume=11
 |location=Москва
 |publisher=Издательство иностранной литературы
 |language=ru
 |trans-title=Tamm–Dancoff method
}}</ref>

In 1956 the Institute of Nuclear Problems was united with the Electrophysical Laboratory of [[Vladimir Veksler]] in Dubna to form the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]], and Yuri Yappa continued to work in this new institution. However, owing to personal circumstances, he discontinued the work in Dubna and in 1957 started to work at the chair of theoretical physics of the Physical Faculty of the Leningrad University. After the chair had split, in the 1970s–1990s he continued at the chair of the theory of [[Atomic nucleus|nucleus]] and [[elementary particles]] (nowadays the chair of high-energy and elementary particle physics<ref>[http://hep.spbu.ru/index.php Site of the Chair of High Energy and Elementary Particle Physics of the Saint-Petersburg State University]</ref>).

Yuri Yappa was a senior research scientist ({{langx|ru|старший научный сотрудник}}) since 1956 and an [[assistant professor]] ({{langx|ru|доцент}}) since 1968. He published over 40 papers on [[quantum field theory]], [[General Relativity]], [[mathematics]], and [[philosophy of science]].

== Scientific work and teaching ==
Yuri Yappa led a number of theoretical courses in the Leningrad/St.-Petersburg University, including his well-known courses of [[General Relativity]], which was passed to him by Vladimir Fock in 1958, and of [[classical electrodynamics]], which served the base of his graduate book (coauthored by Viktor Novozhilov) ''Electrodynamics'',<ref name="electro">{{cite book
 |author=Новожилов Ю. В. |author2=Яппа Ю. А.
 |year=1978
 |script-title=ru:Электродинамика
 |location=Москва
 |publisher=Наука
 |language=ru
 |trans-title=Electrodynamics
}}</ref> whose revised edition was published and republished in English.<ref name="electro-en">{{cite book
 |author=Novozhilov Yu. V. |author2=Yappa Yu. A.
 |orig-date=1981 |year=1986
 |edition=Revised
 |others=Translated from Russian by V. I. Kisin
 |title=Electrodynamics
 |url=https://archive.org/details/NovozhilovYappaElectrodynamics
 |location=Moscow
 |publisher=[[Mir Publishers]]
}}</ref> His graduate text on the theory of [[spinor]]s was finished by his university colleagues and published posthumously.<ref>{{cite book
 |author=Яппа Ю. А.
 |year=2004
 |script-title=ru:Введение в теорию спиноров и её приложения в физике
 |others=Под ред. и с дополнением В. А. Франке
 |location=Санкт-Петербург
 |publisher=Издательство Петербургского университета
 |language=ru
 |trans-title=Introduction into the Theory of Spinors and Its Applications in Physics
 |isbn = 978-5-288-01951-7
}}</ref>
